Open-source research software · v0.1.0 engineering preview

From fish videos to scientific trajectories

Analyze aquatic-animal movement with a connected R, Python and JavaScript toolkit: detections and track identities, synchronized multiview geometry, observed 2D/3D trajectories, behavioural analysis, uncertainty, and experimental workflows.

155 documented functions2D + 3D14 function familiesEngineering-qualified preview
Scientific status: this release is engineering-qualified, but biological identity, underwater metrology, fish welfare inference, empirical interval coverage and real actuator safety are not independently certified. See the evidence and limitations.

Discover the research workflows

Conceptual software workflow, not an empirical performance result.

01 · Acquire

Video tracking and identities

GoPro inputs, video PTS, YOLO/ByteTrack integration, tracker exports and manual annotation.

02 · Reconstruct

Multiview 3D and refraction

Stereo rigs, clock diagnostics, Brown correction, air–glass–water optics and geometric correspondence.

03 · Validate

Scientific benchmarks

Detection F1, IDF1, holdout targets, physical XYZ error and source-truth provenance.

04 · Characterize

Movement and schooling

Speed, paths, spatial occupancy, school geometry, 3D scenes and trajectory recurrence.

05 · Model

Behaviour and longitudinal models

Changepoints, Gaussian HMMs, FPCA, functional curves and nested tank/fish models.

06 · Question

Uncertainty-aware inference

Pixel, optical, identity and trajectory perturbations, with explicit model assumptions.

07 · Experiment

Events and independent tanks

Event alignment, tank-replicated summaries and defensible inferential units.

08 · Interact

Animal–Computer Interaction

Telemetry, choices, access inequality and bounded device-control research protocols.

09 · Communicate

Plots, figures and galleries

Demonstration figures, publication storyboards, 3D projections and reproducible graphics.

A visual laboratory

Original scientific illustration. The geometry is schematic, not a measurement from a real tank.

Reproducible first steps 

# Install the preview from its public source repository
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("stefanosbalaskas/AquaTrajectories", ref = "v0.1.0")

library(aquaTrajectories)
x <- aqt_simulate_tracks(n_fish = 5, n_frames = 200)
aqt_plot_paths(x)
kin <- aqt_kinematics(x, max_gap_s = 0.1)

This simulator produces synthetic random walks, not biologically calibrated fish movement.

Interactive synthetic trajectory explorer

Explore five invented trajectories in synchronized 3D, top, side and front projections with a frame scrubber, playback and individual track toggles. This is a browser-only teaching demonstration, not the actual multiview research explorer or a real animal observation.

Open interactive synthetic explorer

Five complete, runnable publication figures

The five-figure reproducible workbook exercises actual native plotting functions with openly labeled synthetic data for feeding phases, physical XYZ error illustrations, replicated-tank occupancy, event-aligned speed, and heading roses. All five plots include source code and retain their scientific interpretation limits.
